mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active whenever the rate is trending downward, regardless of absolute level.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.0% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 6.0% for 2 consecutive months).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and an increase in consumer spending (measured by RSAFS) signals a coordinated monetary and fiscal stimulus that boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is only active when both conditions occur together.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS decline > 0.05pp and RSAFS increase > 0.1%) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0), the supply chain constraints and reduced manufacturing output signal an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is most active in the late phase of the economic cycle.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is active whenever PAYEMS is trending upward, regardless of absolute level.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS has increased for at least 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 850,000 units, it signals strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, boosting economic growth and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST > 850.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals a robust labor market and strong consumer spending, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is only active when both conditions occur together.
failure_condition: The joint signal (UNRATE decline > 0.1pp and RSAFS increase > 0.2%) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220.0), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is most active in the early phase of a monetary tightening cycle.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 220.0.
